definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined); national character (newer: undefined); native alphanumeric character set (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines 'character' in four senses (in a coded character set, in a screen item, in the COBOL character repertoire, in computer storage) and 'coded character set' as "A set of unambiguous rules that establishes a character set" (taken from ISO/IEC 10646-1); 2023 drops these entries and takes the terms from its normative reference ISO/IEC 10646 (§2023:2), in the same sense. SR16's ordinals count positions in a character set in that sense. 'national character' (§2002:4: "A character in a national character set") is the same notion 2023 uses with its kept 'national character set' entry (§2023:3.125); this compiler's national set is UTF-16 in both editions. 'native alphanumeric character set' (§2002:4: "The computer's alphanumeric coded character set") is 2023's native character set (3.128) restricted to alphanumeric; for this compiler both are UTF-16, so e2)'s 'native alphanumeric ordinal exists' governs the same ordinals; covered at --std 2002 by pb1557/pb1091.

pending-clause.answer: Not dependent: SR16 is a compile-time rule on SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS ordinals; it involves no SIZE ERROR phrase or arithmetic statement (§2002:14.6.4, 14.6.6), and the integer-1 ordinal is a literal, not an arithmetic result.
